pearson.name: Pearson symbol
pearson.text: A short code for the lattice: crystal system (a triclinic, m monoclinic, o orthorhombic, t tetragonal, h hexagonal -- which also covers trigonal and rhombohedral -- and c cubic), centring (P primitive, S side-centred, also written A, B or C, I body-centred, F face-centred, R rhombohedral) and the number of atoms in the conventional cell. cF4 is cubic face-centred with four atoms — aluminium.

prototype.name: Structure type
prototype.text: The known compound whose atomic arrangement this phase shares. Pure aluminium and pure nickel both have the structure type Cu: the same arrangement, a different element. It is not what the phase IS, which is why the search keeps these hits in their own group.

itNumber.name: IT number
itNumber.text: The space group's number in the International Tables for Crystallography, 1 to 230. One group has several written forms (Im-3, Im3, I m -3) and the number has one. It fixes the GROUP, though, not the setting or the origin choice: group 227 comes with two origins whose atom coordinates differ, and one file in this library reports Fd-3m from one data block and Fd-3m O1 from another.

cif.name: CIF
cif.text: Crystallographic Information File: the text file carrying the unit cell, the symmetry and the atom positions. Hough indexing works from it, and everything else here is derived from it.

xtal.name: XTAL
xtal.text: The same structure in EMsoft's own binary form, converted from the CIF. It is the input for a simulation, not for indexing.

master.name: Master pattern
master.text: The simulated diffraction sphere for one phase, computed from the XTAL over a RANGE of beam energies -- Monte Carlo bins up to the accelerating voltage -- and stored as an energy-binned stack. Dictionary indexing weights or picks from those bins and projects the result onto the detector.

sht.name: SHT
sht.text: The master pattern as spherical harmonic coefficients. Spherical indexing correlates against this compact form rather than against the full sphere.

ht.name: ht
ht.text: The high-temperature modification of a phase, in the naming SpringerMaterials uses (rt room temperature, lt low temperature). One phase here carries it: Fe1.8Al4.4Si0.6 ht.

placements.name: Placements
placements.text: A phase appears once in every alloy system it belongs to, so the band view shows more cards than there are phases: 36 phases here, 93 cards. An Al-Fe-Si phase is in all three of those bands, and filing it under one of them would be a decision this library has no business making for you.

labelOnly.name: by name only
labelOnly.text: A hit that matched the phase's NAME but not its structure. `beta-AlFeSi` is named for silicon and the structure in its file contains none -- so a search for Al-Fe-Si finds it and says why, while the silicon facet, which counts structures, does not.
